findings.text: non-blocking: _decode_payload repeats the _PAYLOAD_REGION key construction and lookup that _index_payload already performs at :1704-1712, so one cache has two owners and a change to the key has to be made in both places or the two readers disagree.

non-blocking: the parity check compares the shared-decode batch against the head revision with the region removed (reuse=False), not against the base revision's code the done_when names, so a behaviour change from any other part of this diff would be invisible to it.

non-blocking: the landed record describes 'a second reuse region' for the decoded payload, but the payload cache is a second ContextVar inside the one index_reuse region; a reader taking the fragment literally would nest a region and get different sharing.

non-blocking: inside a region every picker-only read now selects the full payload column and projects it, forfeiting the picker-column optimisation for any region whose reads are all picker-only; no such region exists today, but the trade is not stated at the line.

item_verdicts.call_sites: six production call sites reach the changed ledger readers; reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:_queue_dispatch_batch is the one this diff adds a region to and the other five read through load(), which now shares the decoded payload inside any open region.
item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 2269d5003c; one commit, four files, 437 insertions and 10 deletions, every path inside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_a_batch_decodes_the_ledger_index_once.py, a 200-row ledger, ten entries over three plans, at-most-once counters, a negative control at ten or more decodes and an all_debug batch timing; the manifest records each of those results and the run directory holds the logs.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that every ledger read inside one batch dispatch be answered from a single index decode; reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:1132 wraps queue_batch in one ledger.index_reuse() region and reckon/ledger.py:1704 shares the decoded payload across read shapes inside it.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records 54 passed at head and 51 passed at base with EXIT=0, the negative control at 11 decodes over 10 entries with EXIT=1, the 1.59 measured ratio at 10,300 rows, and a clean worktree at a5ea48f256.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's declared paths and dispatch-detail.json; the declared scope is reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py, reckon/ledger.py, tests/test_a_batch_decodes_the_ledger_index_once.py and the node's evidence fragment.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_batch_decodes_the_ledger_index_once.py:277 reddens when the region is removed (11 decodes, logs/negative-control.log), so it guards the production region at reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:1132.
justifications.evidence: tests/test_a_batch_decodes_the_ledger_index_once.py:277 asserts at most one _index_payload decode and :325 asserts the per-entry behaviour is real, and :298 compares the per-entry outcomes against the region-removed run.
justifications.fit: reckon/ledger.py:1704 re-implements the region-key lookup that _decode_payload already performs at :1771, so one cache has two owners.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:1132 opens one ledger.index_reuse() around queue_batch, and the decodes fall from one per entry to one for the whole batch.
justifications.reuse: the change extends the existing index_reuse region and picker_record projection rather than adding a parallel cache; a search of reckon/ found no other owner of a decoded ledger payload.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff 2269d5003c..a5ea48f256 changes exactly the four declared paths and nothing else.
